cases.sentence: В голосе, как и во взгляде, была мягкость и серьезность, подобная той, которая бывает у людей, постоянно сосредоточенных над одним ___.
cases.explain: «любимым делом» — after the preposition «над», the instrumental marks the means, company, or complement.
cases.translation: When they had set off on foot ahead of the others, and had come out of sight of the house onto the beaten dusty road, marked with rusty wheels and sprinkled with grains of corn, she clung faster to his arm and pressed it closer to her. He had quite forgotten the momentary unpleasant impression, and alone with her he felt, now that the thought of her approaching motherhood was never for a moment absent from his mind, a new and delicious bliss, quite pure from all alloy of sense, in the being near to the woman he loved. There was no need of speech, yet he longed to hear the sound of her voice, which like her eyes had changed since she had been with child. In her voice, as in her eyes, there was that softness and gravity which is found in people continually concentrated on some cherished pursuit.

cases.sentence: – Нет, я так рада случаю побыть с тобою наедине, и признаюсь, как ни хорошо мне с ними, жалко наших ___ вдвоем.
cases.explain: «зимних вечеров» — the genitive here marks possession, absence, or quantity.
cases.translation: “No, I’m so glad of a chance of being alone with you, and I must own, though I’m happy with them, I do regret our winter evenings alone.”

cases.sentence: Левин уже привык теперь смело говорить свою мысль, не давая себе труда облекать ее в ___; он знал, что жена в такие любовные минуты, как теперь, поймет, что он хочет сказать, с намека, и она поняла его.
cases.explain: «точные слова» — after the preposition «в», the accusative marks the direct object of the verb.
cases.translation: Levin had grown used by now to uttering his thought boldly, without taking the trouble of clothing it in exact language. He knew that his wife, in such moments of loving tenderness as now, would understand what he meant to say from a hint, and she did understand him.

cases.sentence: Левин уже привык теперь смело говорить свою мысль, не давая себе труда облекать ее в точные слова; он знал, что жена в такие ___, как теперь, поймет, что он хочет сказать, с намека, и она поняла его.
cases.explain: «любовные минуты» — after the preposition «в», the accusative marks the direct object of the verb.
cases.translation: Levin had grown used by now to uttering his thought boldly, without taking the trouble of clothing it in exact language. He knew that his wife, in such moments of loving tenderness as now, would understand what he meant to say from a hint, and she did understand him.

cases.sentence: Она никак не могла бы выразить тот ход мыслей, который заставлял ее улыбаться; но ___ был тот, что муж ее, восхищающийся братом и унижающий себя пред ним, был неискренен.
cases.explain: «последний вывод» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: She could never have explained the chain of thought that made her smile; but the last link in it was that her husband, in exalting his brother and abasing himself, was not quite sincere. Kitty knew that this insincerity came from his love for his brother, from his sense of shame at being too happy, and above all from his unflagging craving to be better—she loved it in him, and so she smiled.

cases.sentence: – Ну, что ты скажешь про папа? – спросила Кити. – Что же, и он плох, потому что ничего не делал для ___?
cases.explain: «общего дела» — after the preposition «для», the genitive here marks possession, absence, or quantity.
cases.translation: “Well, what would you say about papa?” asked Kitty. “Is he a poor creature then, as he does nothing for the public good?”

cases.sentence: – Сделает, не сделает, – говорил Левин, обрывая белые узкие ___.
cases.explain: «продороженные лепестки» — the accusative marks the direct object of the verb.
cases.translation: “He does, he doesn’t,” said Levin, tearing off the white petals.
